value: A positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom
reasoning: In Rutherford's experiment most alpha-particles passed straight through the foil but a very small fraction were deflected through large angles, which is only possible if the atom's positive charge and almost all its mass are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.
Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers; argon (Z = 18) and calcium (Z = 20) both have mass number 40, whereas the other pairs share the same atomic number and so are isotopes.

value: Copper displacing lead from lead chloride is not feasible
reasoning: A metal can displace another from its salt only if it is more reactive; copper lies below lead in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace lead, while iron, zinc and magnesium all lie above copper and displace it from copper sulphate.
The pH scale runs from 0 to 14 with 7 as neutral, so pH 0 corresponds to a hydrogen-ion concentration of 1 mol/L, the strongest acidity on the scale.
The parietal cells of the gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid, which makes the stomach medium acidic, kills ingested microbes and activates pepsinogen into pepsin.

value: Boric acid–antiseptic, citric acid–food preservative, magnesium hydroxide–antacid, acetic acid–pickle
reasoning: Boric acid is a mild antiseptic used in eye washes, citric acid is a common food preservative and acidulant, magnesium hydroxide is milk of magnesia used as an antacid, and acetic acid as vinegar is used in pickles.
Pitch is the perception of how shrill or flat a sound is, and it rises with the frequency of the wave; amplitude determines loudness, not pitch.

value: X-rays being deflected by electric fields is not a property of X-rays
reasoning: X-rays are electrically neutral electromagnetic waves, so they are undeflected by both electric and magnetic fields; their very short wavelength and high penetrating power are genuine properties.

value: The image formed by a plane mirror is not real — it is virtual
reasoning: Light rays only appear to diverge from behind a plane mirror and never actually meet there, so the image is virtual, erect, of the same size and formed as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

A periscope has two plane mirrors fixed at the ends of a tube, each inclined at 45 degrees to the tube axis and therefore parallel to one another, so light reflected from the first travels down the tube and is reflected again to the eye along the original direction.
The refractive index is the ratio of the speed of light in air to that in the medium, so v = c/n = (3 × 10^8)/(3/2) = 2 × 10^8 m/s.
In the electromagnetic spectrum wavelength decreases in the order radio waves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, so ultraviolet has the shortest wavelength of the four listed.
From Hooke's law F = kx, the force constant is force divided by extension, giving units of newton per metre.

Elephantiasis (lymphatic filariasis) develops slowly over years in endemic areas and does not produce sudden outbreaks, whereas cholera, malaria and smallpox spread rapidly through a population and are classic epidemic diseases.
Amphibians such as the salamander have a three-chambered heart with two atria and one ventricle; the shark Scoliodon has a two-chambered heart while birds and mammals have four chambers.

value: Pollination, fertilization, division of zygote, formation of embryo, seedling
reasoning: Pollen must first reach the stigma, the male gamete then fuses with the egg to form a zygote, and only after the zygote divides does the embryo and finally the seedling develop.
Exhaled air is rich in carbon dioxide, which reacts with limewater (calcium hydroxide) to precipitate insoluble calcium carbonate and turn it milky.
Adenosine triphosphate is called the energy currency of the cell because the energy released on breaking its terminal phosphate bond drives most endothermic cellular processes.
Digestion begins in the buccal cavity where saliva mixes with food, so salivary amylase, which starts the breakdown of starch into sugar, is the first digestive enzyme to act.
The Dandi March of 1930 was a protest against the British salt law, and Gandhi broke it by making salt, sodium chloride, from sea water at Dandi.

value: Bleaching powder–CaOCl2, baking soda–NaHCO3, washing soda–Na2CO3·10H2O, slaked lime–Ca(OH)2
reasoning: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, washing soda is the decahydrate of sodium carbonate and slaked lime is calcium hydroxide.
Blue vitriol is copper sulphate pentahydrate, CuSO4·5H2O, and losing these five water molecules on heating turns the blue crystals white.

value: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air to form a black coating of silver sulphide
reasoning: Tarnishing of silver is corrosion by hydrogen sulphide and other sulphur compounds present in air, producing a black layer of silver sulphide on the surface.
The Kelvin and Celsius scales have the same size of degree but their zeros differ by 273, so the Kelvin reading is obtained by adding 273 to the Celsius reading.
From R = ρl/A, resistivity equals resistance times area divided by length, which gives ohm times a unit of length, that is ohm-cm (or ohm-metre in SI).
Satellite communication uses microwave frequencies, which lie within the radio-wave region of the spectrum, because these waves penetrate the ionosphere instead of being reflected back to earth.
Urine formed in the kidneys is carried by the ureters to the urinary bladder, where it is stored, and is finally expelled through the urethra.
The pituitary is a single unpaired gland lying at the base of the brain, whereas the adrenals, testes and ovaries each occur as a pair.
Mitochondria are semi-autonomous organelles carrying their own circular DNA and ribosomes; the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and endoplasmic reticulum contain no genetic material.
Edward Jenner introduced vaccination in 1796 by showing that inoculation with cowpox material protected against smallpox, which founded the practice of immunization.
